newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's food distribution plan not ready yet - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's food distribution plan not ready yet - U.N.

text.p: Iraq has not yet completed its food distribution plan to cover the next six months of oil exports, Iraq's U.N. coordinator Staffan de Mistura said on Thursday.
"It is in the hands of the government," he said.
De Mistura said U.N. relief officials in Baghdad also needed to give their approval before sending the plan to the U.N. Secretary-General for ratification.
Iraq is permitted to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months, under U.N. supervision, to alleviate hardship caused by U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Baghdad for invading Kuwait in 1991.
The oil plan was first started in December last year and the U.N. Security Council renewed it for another 180 days early this month.

De Mistura said the Iraq government's plan will cover the central and southern parts of the country. U.N. relief agencies will prepare a special food distribution plan for the three Kurdish provinces in northern Iraq where rebel Kurds run their own affairs.
In the first six months Iraq earned about $1.3 billion, of which $260 million was earmarked for the northern provinces.
De Mistura said Iraq would earn a similar amount of money in the next six months so he did not think the preparation of distribution plans would face any hurdles.
Iraq and the U.N. had problems reaching a consensus on the type of humanitarian goods to be purchased, which delayed oil sales for at least two months.
Iraq has not yet started oil exports for the second six months. It is not clear whether the go-head for the exports needs U.N. ratification of the new food distribution plans for Iraq.
Senior Iraqi officials have frequently complained about the delay in implementing the distribution plan for the first six months.

Health Minister Umeed Mubarak in remarks published in Baghdad newspapers on Wednesday said Iraq had received only $2 million worth of medicines from the $210 million allocated for medical purchases in the first distribution plan.
Food supplies reaching Iraq so far have totalled about 800,000 tonnes, mostly wheat and rice, out of the more than two million tonnes Iraq had contracted for.
